You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

[HarnessEntry(id='arc_stamp_motif_on_exact_zero_shape_matches', kind='memory', title='ARC: stamp motif on exact zero-shape matches', content="For ARC grids with a sparse colored motif embedded in a noisy 0/background-color field, a task may ask to find every translation where the motif's colored-cell mask lands entirely on zeros, then recolor those zero cells with the motif color. Preserve the original motif and every nonmatching cell. Match the original orientation only; do not rotate or reflect unless demos show otherwise. Ignore motif bounding-box cells that are not colored: the match condition is that all motif cells land on 0, not that the whole bounding box matches a fixed pattern. Overlapping matches should produce the union of their motif cells. Demonstrated with a 3-colored 4x5 mask: two same-orientation placements on zeros were recolored, including overlaps, and output differences exactly equaled the union. Another 6-cell 1 mask in a 0/9 field had three placements; the output was the motif color at all their cells. Previous examples also confirmed no rotated/reflected matches. Use demos to verify target background, motif color, and whether orientation changes are allowed. Practical caution: transcribing a grid with even one omitted cell can hide a valid match and produce an invalid-sized output; verify every row has the stated width before matching and before submission. Confirmed again in task-58fa3f1c: a sparse 8-cell color-5 mask in a noisy 0/9 grid had exactly two translations whose mask cells were all 0; stamp 5 on both, preserve the original motif and all other cells.

Another accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c): on a 29x11 grid with background 6, scattered zero cells, and an 8-shaped L triomino with mask offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)}, the rule was to stamp 8 over every translation whose three mask positions were all originally 0. There were 25 placements; preserve all 6s and unmatched 0s and take the union if placements overlap. This confirms the rule also applies when the nonzero background is 6 and the motif has only three colored cells. Compute matches from the original grid, not incrementally from already-stamped cells.", path='arc-patterns', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T08:42:09.205188+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T09:01:06.477604+00:00', version=4), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_8a59eaa1_repeat_motif_across_divider_separated_panels', kind='memory', title='ARC task-8a59eaa1: repeat motif across divider-separated panels', content="For ARC task-8a59eaa1, color-3 full rows/columns divide a grid into equal panels (in the demo, a full color-3 row and column made four equal quadrants). The rule generalizes to 30x30 -> 10x10 as well as the smaller grids noted above.", path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T10:20:56.555363+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T11:59:24.245639+00:00', version=3), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_7064b436_fill_gaps_in_broken_rectangle_border_with_2', kind='memory', title='ARC task-7064b436: fill gaps in broken rectangle border with 2', content='For task-7064b436, the grid has a large axis-aligned rectangular outline in a foreground color (demo: 3 on background 6; test: 5 on 7), with missing cells along its four sides. Added after validating demos: other examples show a border can be complete while an internal repeated-marker line still needs bridging.', path='arc-patterns', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={'task_id': 'task-7064b436'}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T11:05:43.708478+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T11:58:39.279042+00:00', version=7), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_b0146853_move_object_against_divider_and_add_8_line', kind='memory', title='ARC task-b0146853: move object against divider and add 8-line', content='For ARC task-b0146853: Grid has uniform background, a full horizontal or vertical divider line (color 2 in demos), and a non-background object on one side.
